Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Consultant will also indicate potential cost/time impacts by clicking here Consultant will also provide a description of the cost/time impact under the details tab. This description will not be visible to the contractor. The Consultant will then click Proceed to Next Workflow Step. These check boxes are not visible to the Contractor ese check boxes are not visible to the Contractor IF CONSULTANT INDICATE THERE IS A COST IMPACT: The Actioners can then mark Workflow Complete and the response is issued to the Contractor but they will not be informed of the potential cost impact. If the Actioners deem that there is indeed a cost impact, then the Contracts Manager can proceed to Generate a Change Event. If the cost impact check box is marked then, the workflow proceeds to the 1st branch containing the Delivery, Design and st branch containing the Delivery, Design and Construction managers (Actioners). This will also send out a cc notification to the Contracts, Cost and Planning managers as well as the estimators. The Actioners can review the consultant response and must indicate explicitly whether there is a cost impact or not by Writing Yes/No in the Cost Impact field in the header info. This field is mandatory and you cannot save the record without filling it. IF CONSULTANT DOESN’T INDICATE A COST IMPACT: it. IF CONSULTANT DOESN’T INDICATE A COST IMPACT: If the Consultant doesn’t mark the Cost impact check box the workflow proceeds to the 2nd branch containing the Delivery, Design and Construction managers (Actioners). This will NOT send out a cc notification to the Contracts, Cost and Planning managers as well as the estimators. The Actioners can review the consultant response and must indicate explicitly whether there is a cost must indicate explicitly whether there is a cost impact or not by Writing Yes/No in the Cost Impact field in the header info. If the Actioners deem that THERE IS A POTENTIAL COST IMPACT, they can either return it to the consultant with comments (marked in the Cost Impact Description box under Details so that contractor cannot view it) or Action it themselves and notify the Contracts Manager to Generate a Change Event.

Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

14.6 Issue of Interim Payment Certificates (a) the Contractor has: (i) kept satisfactory records (including the orders, receipts, Costs and use of Plant and Materials) which are available for inspection, and (ii) submitted a statement of the Cost of acquiring and delivering the Plant and Materials to the Site, supported by satisfactory evidence; and either: (b) the relevant Plant and Materials: (i) are those listed in the Appendix to Tender for payment when shipped, (ii) have been shipped to the Country, en route to the Site, in accordance with the Contract; and (iii) are described in a clean shipped bill of lading or other evidence of shipment, which has been submitted to the Engineer together with evidence of payment of freight and insurance, any other documents reasonably required, and a bank guarantee in a form and issued by an entity approved by the Employer in amounts and currencies equal to the amount due under this Sub-Clause: this guarantee may be in a similar form to the form referred to in Sub-Clause 14.2 [Advance Payment] and shall be valid until the Plant and Materials are properly stored on Site and protected against loss, damage or deterioration; or (c) the relevant Plant and Materials: (i) are those listed in the Appendix to Tender for payment when delivered to the Site, and (ii) have been delivered to and are properly stored on the Site, are protected against loss, damage or deterioration, and appear to be in accordance with the Contract. The additional amount to be certified shall be the equivalent of eighty percent of the Engineer’s determination of the cost of the Plant and Materials (including delivery to Site), taking account of the documents mentioned in this Sub-Clause and of the contract value of the Plant and Materials. The currencies for this additional amount shall be the same as those in which payment will become due when the contract value is included under sub-paragraph (a) of Sub- Clause 14.3 [Application for Interim Payment Certificates]. At that time, the Payment Certificate shall include the applicable reduction which shall be equivalent to, and in the same currencies and proportions as, this additional amount for the relevant Plant and Materials. No amount will be certified or paid until the Employer has received and approved the Performance Security. Thereafter, the Engineer shall, within 28 days after receiving a Statement and supporting documents, issue to the Employer an Interim Payment Certificate which shall state the amount which the Engineer fairly determines to be due, with supporting particulars. However, prior to issuing the Taking-Over Certificate for the Works, the Engineer shall not be bound to issue an Interim Payment Certificate in an amount which would (after retention and other deductions) be less than the minimum amount of Interim Payment Certificates (if any) stated in the Appendix to Tender. In this event, the Engineer shall give notice to the Contractor accordingly. 14.7 Payment 14.8 Delayed Payment

Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

# Saudi Building Code (SBC) — Structure & Application General-knowledge reference on the Saudi Building Code (SBC): what it is, how the series is organized, who maintains it, and how it is applied in the design and approval of construction in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Titles below are drawn from published SBC references. ## What the SBC is The Saudi Building Code is the Kingdom's mandatory technical code governing theKingdom's mandatory technical code governing the design, construction, alteration, and use of buildings and their systems. It is adopted so that building-permit approval and design review are measured against a single national technical baseline covering structural safety, fire and life safety, electrical and mechanical systems, energy, and plumbing. - Maintained by: the Saudi Building Code National Committee (SBCNC; sbc.gov.sa).ding Code National Committee (SBCNC; sbc.gov.sa). - Basis: the SBC is developed with reference to leading international codes and standards (e.g. the ICC family and NFPA), adapted to Saudi conditions, materials, and climate. - Editions: the code is issued in dated editions — a 2018 edition and a later 2024 edition of the code and its requirements/commentary documents are published; always design to the edition in force for the jurisdiction andto the edition in force for the jurisdiction and project, confirming which edition a given municipality currently enforces. ## Role in the approval lifecycle - SBC compliance is a precondition of the municipal building permit ("rukhsa"); design submissions to the municipality/Balady are reviewed against it. - Licensed engineering offices are responsible for producing SBC-compliant design and, in many cases, supervising construction to the code.many cases, supervising construction to the code. - The fire volume (SBC 801) is the technical basis for Civil Defense (Salamah) fire and life-safety approval; the energy volume underpins energy compliance; the plumbing and structural volumes govern their respective trades. ## Series structure The SBC is published as a family of numbered volumes. The commonly cited structure is:mbered volumes. The commonly cited structure is: - SBC 201 — General: the general/administrative and architectural requirements that frame the code (published across multiple volumes). - SBC 301 — Structural: loading and forces (loads/actions on structures). - SBC 302 — Structural: construction, testing, and inspection requirements (published references cite this volume as the construction / testing and inspection code). - SBC 303 — Structural: soils and foundations.). - SBC 303 — Structural: soils and foundations. - SBC 304 — Structural: concrete structures. - SBC 305 — Structural: masonry structures. - SBC 306 — Structural: steel structures. - SBC 401 — Electrical. - SBC 501 — Mechanical (including HVAC). - SBC 601 — Energy Conservation (general/non-residential). - SBC 602 — Energy Conservation (residential / low-rise). - SBC 701 — Plumbing (Saudi Plumbing Code; water supply and drainage). - SBC 702 — Private sewage disposal / on-site sewage.C 702 — Private sewage disposal / on-site sewage. - SBC 801 — Fire Protection (published across multiple volumes). - SBC 901 — Existing Buildings (retrofit, alteration, and renovation). - SBC 1001 — Green Construction (sustainable/green building requirements). - SBC 1101 / 1102 — Residential Building Code (residential design

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.

  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

ALJAZZAR g) ip ot I MOHAMMED OMAR JAZZAR CONSULTING ENGINEERS CO Auwsigl GILaiuS Ne ae dane AS yc 1. Statement of Problem Urban infrastructures are becoming more complex last century. The importance of pipe detecting and the value of its application. Before excavation for maintenance of underground piping, it is necessary to understand the various site problems on topography and surface materials (e.g. position (depth and displacement) and size of other piping, as well as manholes); In order to prevent third party companies from possible damages to infrastructural equipments and people, severe damage will be generated from mistaken excavation of other piping. The severity might even affect the corporate image and living resources such as electricity, telecommunication and hydrology. Detection of underground pipeline and cable locations is very important, in addition, locations and positions of infrastructural elements with respect to each other must be known for the new infrastructural projects and for the process of operation and replacement of current infrastructure. 1.1. Introduction Developing Technologies are rapidly, so there are a lot of devices for the detection of pipeline and cable locations. These devices are working with two methods in general. One of them is electromagnetic detection method with electromagnetic induction, and the other is GPR (Ground Penetrating Radar) method working with the principle of determining the underground structure and underground holes. Especially with the new instruments and computer algorithms developed in the last years, the locations of infrastructural elements with respect to each other are determined more accurately. Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method that uses radar pulses to image the subsurface. This non-destructive method uses electromagnetic (EM) radiation in the microwave band (UHF/VHF frequencies) of the radio spectrum, and detects the reflected signals from subsurface structures. One of the most useful applications of GPR in urban infrastructural engineering is mapping and detection of buried pipes. This unique application becomes imperative due to the ever-growing urbanization in both developed and developing nations with its attendant demand for buried utilities. The construction, development and management of subsurface infrastructures has become a very viable business that attracts the attention of scientists and engineers over the past few years. Various utilities such as telecommunication and electric power cables, water and gas supply cables etc. are delivered through underground pipes of various sized buried at different depths. In many cases, maintenance of these infrastructures requires digging operation which leads to unintentional damage to some of the facilities. - Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.
